output.brief: The slowdown comes from one change, not from Corvane or the new hires. Credit Policy v14 took effect on 1 May. It requires a full inspection appraisal for property collateral above $150k, where the old threshold was $500k. Full appraisals take about 8.6 days at the valuation firm. Desktop valuations take about 1.2 days. Full appraisals rose from about 30 a month to about 80. Property-secured loans show the valuation stage going from 1.6 to 8.4 days. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, and consumer loans on Corvane are unchanged. Document collection at the new-hire branches matches the other branches. The valuation firm's turnaround per type of valuation hasn't changed. The policy's impact on processing times was never assessed. Withdrawals may be partly an artefact of the 30-day auto-close rule, so I can't say the delay caused them. I'm fairly confident of the cause. Next steps: take the measured delay and the audit rationale (desktop values ran 12% high) to the credit risk committee, for example to consider a middle band or a faster appraisal route. Add a by-stage view to the dashboard. Don't withhold the Corvane payment or put the new hires on improvement plans. Check withdrawal closure codes before spending on win-back offers.
